steps.text: Combine honey, 1 cup sugar, and water in a saucepan; bring to a simmer and cook 5 minutes. Stir in lemon juice; bring to a boil and cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool while you prepare the cake.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9-inch square baking pan.
Combine flour, baking powder, orange zest, cinnamon, and salt in a bowl; set aside.

Beat remaining 3/4 cup sugar and butter together in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time. Beat in flour mixture, alternating with milk, beating just until incorporated; stir in walnuts. Pour batter into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean, about 40 minutes.

Remove cake from oven and poke holes over the surface with a toothpick. Slowly ladle the cooled honey syrup over cake. For best results, set cake aside for 4 to 6 hours to cool and absorb the syrup before slicing and serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Honey Cake
raw_recipe.description: This Greek honey cake recipe yields a very moist cake permeated with orange and lemon flavors. It is loaded with walnuts and soaked in a honey syrup.

review.reviewBody: I've made this cake on several occasions and it was a hit each time. My only recommendation is to spare the honey dressing - if you use all that is recommended, you'll end up with honey soup with cake in it. I typically use about half of what is prepared.

this came out just as amazing as I thought it would! I added lemon zest instead of orange. I cut the syrup recipe by half and I used mostly honey and about a quarter of the white sugar. Added like 2-3 tablespoons of lemon juice to the syrup and it is just amazing!!!!! I used a round pan and it looks just like the main picture :) this will be made OFTEN!!! I just ate 4 pieces!! ***** This is an update!! this third time making this I decided to use honey instead of the sugar in the cake itself since the name is Honey Cake, not granulated sugar cake... it was so moist from this that I didn't need to add the milk. For the syrup I used about a cup of honey with like 5 tablespoons (a splash) of orange juice and one tablespoon of sugar and it is so good!! the best one yet!

This might be one of the best tasting cakes I've ever had. The flavor is just phenomenal, and the cake itself is super moist from the honey syrup--it's divine! My changes were to up the salt in the cake to 3/4 tsp, and to use half pistachios and half walnuts. For the honey syrup, I took the advice of the other reviewers to halve it, and to add orange juice to it. I also only added about 2 tbsps of the white sugar. That made plenty of syrup, and made the cake sweet without it being tooth-achingly so. I let the cake sit for about 10-15 minutes before I cut it and poured the honey syrup on. Next time I might let the cake cool fully before cutting it--as it kind of got tore up, even with using a super sharp knife to cut it. I think cooling it will allow the cake to hold it's shape a little better. Other than that, this cake is excellent with a cup of coffee or espresso; and keeps well for several days! Highly recommend giving this one a try! Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Yes! This recipe is the one I have been searching for! I have been looking for a recipe similar to the cakes I used to buy in Kardamena, on the island of Kos. 
It is sticky, moist, citrusy, and very sweet. The taste is truly phenomenal!

I have made it three times now, and here are my notes:
1. My favourite version uses half the syrup. I have made it both ways, and feel the recipe as is is too "wet".
2. Greek desserts are small, as rhey are so decadently sweet and rich. As such, I got 24 portions out of the recipe, not 12. 
3. Before adding the walnuts, toast them first. I do this in a dry frying pan, on medium high heat. Shake constantly until they smell fragrant. This releases more walnut oil, and gives a more nutty fragrance to the finished product.

I love the simplicity of this cake and have tried several variations as noted below. I save about half of the syrup to use again on a second cake to gift to friends. I have made it most often as muffins in paper cups often adding golden raisins and semi sweet chocolate chips in addition to chopped walnuts. I also add a hint of vanilla and almond extract to the syrup, substitute condensed milk or Greek 2% yogurt for the milk and add other spices typically nutmeg and allspice to the cinnamon. Great to warm up in the morning as a breakfast muffin.

This was really good! I made a few changes for taste:
-I added some extra orange zest to the cake itself because the orange flavor was a little weak. I also added some honey (maybe around 1 1/2 teaspoons) to the cake for extra honey flavor.
-I changed the cake to muffins because I didn't have the pan for it (it made 15 muffins, baked at 330 degrees for 35 minutes) and it turned out fine.
-I halved the amount of honey syrup because the recipe makes a lot of it and I didn't want as much. I also added a bit of cinnamon on top after I drizzled the honey syrup.
Overall it was really good and also really fun to make! It turned out delicious and I loved it :-)

I made this for a Greek dinner at a friends house. My husband and I took a little taste test and love it. Yummy and moist. In place of the water I used fresh orange juice in the syrup. Love the orange flavor.

My son requested a Greek meal for his birthday dinner and so we made this for his birthday cake. I forgot to put the walnuts in but sprinkled them on top after the cake started baking. Even so, it was amazing, tasted like baklava cake. I did substitute a gluten free all-purpose flour with no problem and baked it in a 9" springform pan (which I placed on a deep serving plate before pouring the syrup in case the seal on the pan wasn't good). So glad to have found something that tastes like baklava that's gluten free!

Truly delicious! Really does remind me of baklava except this is so much easier to make. Because of a walnut allergy, I use pecans that I bake about five minutes as the oven is warming up and then chop. I use an 8x11 1/2" glass cake pan which results in a height similar to baklava, so the pieces nicely soak up the honey syrup of which I use about 3/4 of the syrup recipe (with a bit more fresh lemon juice to cut the sweetness perfectly). The rest of the syrup goes into a little pitcher for anyone who wants extra. I love this recipe!

I really like this recipe. Easier than baklava and has a flavor of it's own. It is a smallish, moist, dense cake, but that works well because it is quite rich. I made it a day ahead. I followed the suggestions of other reviewers to double the cinnamon and add a pinch of nutmeg. I also took the suggestion to eliminate the sugar from the glaze one step further and (subbed orange blossom honey for regular) heated in the microwave for 30 seconds and then drizzled it straight from the bottle onto the individual pieces. It worked well as then people were able decide for themselves how much they wanted and it was easy for me to prep and clean up. Definitely give this one a try!

AMAZING! I used honey instead of the white sugar and instead of milk, I just added a few large dollops of Greek Yogurt. I also skipped the orange flavor and went with all lemon. I squeezed a whole lemon in there as well as the lemon zest I could scrape off. For the topping, I did only the honey with a bit of water to burn off and again, more lemon juice. I only poured on 1/3rd as other readers said to watch the portioning. I jarred the rest and put on the table for others to add as they liked. I also topped it with some lemon zest and served it with a bit of Greek yogurt.

Pretty good in terms of flavor. Wish the cake was thicker - maybe double it or use a smaller baking pan. I should have trusted the recipe instead of the reviews in terms of the honey syrup. I cut the honey syrup down to about half the honey and a quarter of the sugar. I understand the impulse because even putting that much on the cake I was panicking that it was too much, but you gotta trust the process because all of that soaks right in over the next hour or so and it probably would have been nice with more. Without any of the syrup it would have been a little plain, like a coffee cake instead of a dessert.
It was difficult. If you read the reviews there were too many revisions. Maybe put out anew recipe?

Okay, to be honest this is AMAZINGLY GOOD!!!! My husband made this for me (I suffer from chronic back and am disabled) so, I loved the smell of the house when he was making it. He did say the only downside (which he said he didn't want to downgrade to 4 stars because it's so good) is that when he made the recipe according to directions, he didn't realize that the cake would literally be so small. He did say that next time he makes it, he is going to double the ingredients so that there is "more" cake. The sweetness that is ladled over the top of the cake, OMG, is out of this world. He had so much of it leftover, he put it in a small freezer bag for next time when he bakes. For all of you that do not eat honey, sugar you can use the alternatives to this. Also, with the butter, it says to use 3/4 cup unsalted butter and he used 1/2 cup butter and 1/4 cup no sugar applesauce. He said that instead of using orange zest, which we didn't have at the time, he used sugar free apricot preserves. This is a great dessert to take anywhere, simple to follow the directions and the dessert itself is mind blowing. Good luck all!!
I used pecans because I had on hand. I didn’t use all of the honey glaze trying to decrease the sugar content.

I definitely agree with other reviewers that there was waaaay too much syrup to cake ratio. Even halving the syrup in the recipe, it was a very messy affair, with syrup leaking everywhere out of the cake. The flavor was alright, if somewhat one-note of just sugary-ness. It came out a bit more dense than I usually prefer my cakes as well.

As at least one other commentor has mentioned, the recipe for the dressing/sauce makes more than necessary - by a factor of two. However, it's so much better than simple syrup that I'm going to make just the sauce and keep it for hot toddies this winter.
